newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FERRUM STEEL MILL CLEARED FOR PUBLIC TRADE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FERRUM STEEL MILL CLEARED FOR PUBLIC TRADE.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) cleared an initial public offering of up to three million shares of steel mill Ferrum SA, the commission chairman Jacek Socha told a news briefing on Thursday.
He said the commission also approved 4,314,000 existing shares of Ferrum, which wants to seek the Warsaw bourse's main market listing.
The company will offer 2.4 million shares in the large investor tranche due on February 11-12 and 600,000 shares in the small investor tranche scheduled for February 12-17.
The issue will be valid if investors subscribe for at least 2,950,000 shares.

In the large investor tranche investors can register for at least 50,000 shares and no more than 500,000 shares. In the small investor tranche investors can subscribe for no fewer than 10 shares and no more than 10,000 shares.
Ferrum's main shareholders are National Investment Fund No 1, which has a 33-percent stake and the state treasury which has a 25.1 percent stake.
Ferrum had a net profit of 3.2 million zlotys last year on 161.1-million-zloty sales.

It expects its net to fall to 2.9 million zlotys in 1996 and to rebound to 3.3 million zlotys in 1997. Its sales were expected to fall to 147.8 million zlotys this year and pickup to 164.8 million zlotys in 1997.
